title: Reservation timeline editor and priority rules - draft
body:
Context and goal:
This doc is a working draft that sketches an interactive timeline-based reservation editor for Dedicated capacity. Primary goals:
- Make it trivial for platform engineers and ops to create timeboxed reservations across GPU pools with fine-grained priority and SLA settings.
- Surface conflicts, cost impact, and preemption risk up front.
- Let users combine recurring reservations, ad-hoc bursts, and reserved capacity into a single visual timeline.

Why a timeline?
Current reservation flows are form-heavy and hard to reason about when multiple reservations overlap or when autoscale/burst budgets interact. A timeline gives immediate visual feedback on overlap, capacity headroom, and cost curves across time.

User personas and stories (short):
- Platform engineer (Day-to-day): "I need to reserve 4 A100s for a performance test next Tuesday from 08:00-20:00 with high-priority so it won't be preempted by spot jobs."
- ML infra lead: "Show me the monthly recurring production training window and how bursts scheduled this week will eat into my monthly burst budget."
- Solutions engineer: "Create a canary reservation that escalates to full capacity after validation (canary -> ramp -> steady)."

Key interactions and wireframe notes:
1) Header: pool selector + SLA tier chips + timezone selector.
   - Pool selector shows GPU type icons and pool labels (e.g., "dedicated-a100-pool-east-1").
   - SLA chips: Standard / Priority / Preemptible (preemptible shows a warning icon).
2) Timeline canvas: horizontal time axis (week/day/hour zoom).
   - Lanes per resource group: one lane per GPU type or per pool. Lane shows total capacity bar on left.
   - Reservations rendered as colored blocks with labels (name, vCPUs/GPUs allocated). Blocks have drag handles for start/end and can be resized or nudged.
   - Overlap highlighter: when two reservations overlap and exceed capacity, the overlapping area flashes amber/red with tooltip to explain conflict.
   - Cost overlay toggle: show estimated $/hour as a thin, semi-transparent band behind the timeline.
3) Reservation detail sheet (right rail): editable fields (name, owner, recurrence, start/end, quantity, SLA, preemptible toggle, cost estimate, tags).
   - Quick actions: Convert to recurring, Add burst window, Add rollback anchor.
4) Priority rules editor (modal or inline):
   - Numeric priority (0-100) + policy dropdown (strict, fair-share, weighted).
   - Fallbacks: if higher-priority request arrives and capacity shortfall occurs, system suggests automatic fallback (scale down preemptible non-prod) or notify.
5) Burst and budget meter (top-right): shows monthly burst budget used vs remaining; clicking shows a breakdown of burst consumption by reservation.
6) Autoscale anchors: small vertical markers that indicate when autoscale policies will trigger based on queued requests or latency SLO breaches. Hover shows policy details.

Edge cases / subtleties to call out:
- Timezone handling: reservations created in different timezones should show both creator timezone and pool local timezone in the detail sheet.
- Recurring reservations across DST boundaries: show a warning if recurrence moves by an hour.
- Partial fulfillment: if capacity is partially available, the system should allow a partial reservation (e.g., 3/4 GPUs guaranteed, remainder best-effort). UI must show what is guaranteed vs best-effort.
- Cross-pool cascades: if pool A is full but pool B is compatible (same architecture but slightly higher cost), UI shows a recommended fallback with delta cost.

Backlog grooming (tickets with rough sizing):
- UX-1701: Core timeline canvas + pool-lanes implementation (M).
- UX-1702: Drag/resize interactions + keyboard nudge + snap to 15m increments (S).
- UX-1703: Reservation detail right-rail + save/preview flow (S).
- UX-1704: Conflict detection engine + visual overlay (L).
- UX-1705: Cost overlay & burst budget meter (M).
- UX-1706: Priority rules editor + fallback policy suggestions (L).
- UX-1707: Recurrence editor with DST handling and preview (M).
- UX-1708: Export/CSV and API sync endpoints (S).
- UX-1709: Accessibility pass (keyboard-only, screen reader labels) (S).
- UX-1710: Canary -> ramp -> steady rollout pattern shortcut (S).
Estimates: S=2-3 pts, M=5-8 pts, L=13+ pts.

Acceptance criteria (draft):
- User can create, move, and resize reservations on the timeline and see immediate conflict indicators.
- Reservation detail panel updates live and shows cost estimate.
- Creating a high-priority reservation triggers validation that surfaces any necessary preemption/fallback rules.
- Recurrence preview shows next N instances and flags DST issues.
- Burst budget meter reflects real-time usage for the account.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Should priority be numeric (0-100) or tiered (low/medium/high)? (Pros/cons in notes).
- How aggressive should UI be in suggesting cross-pool fallbacks vs requiring explicit user approval?
- Do we expose cost tradeoffs inline by default or behind a toggle to reduce noise for operator users?
- Should administrators be able to lock lanes to prevent new ad-hoc reservations?

Quick mockup links:
- Figma (working): https://figma.com/file/abcd1234/reservation-editor-v1 (see page: timeline-editor, frames A1-A6)
- Sketch/PNG: (exported frames attached in internal review thread)

Notes from 2025-11-25 sync meeting:
- Liam: push conflict overlay color to amber for soft conflicts and red for hard (hard = >100% overcommit).
- Sofia: requested a "dry-run cost impact" preview that simulates the monthly billing delta if reservation is accepted.
- Rohit: reminded to include an API-first design so automation (terraform/provider) can interact with same primitives as the UI.

Next steps (immediate):
- Resolve "numeric vs tier" priority decision with product and SRE (owner: Priya, due: 2025-12-05).
- UX: produce hi-fi flows for drag/resize, detail pane, and priority editor (owner: Sofia, due: 2025-12-12).
- Eng: spike conflict detection algorithm (owner: Rohit, estimate: 3d).
- Sync with billing on cost model assumptions for the cost overlay (owner: Liam).

Notes-to-self / low-quality fragments (keep; they're helpful):
- Consider small in-timeline microlegend for quick visual mapping (P = preemptible, R = recurring, B = burst).
- Keyboard shortcut: press 'r' to open recurrence modal on selected block.
- Save as template: allow saving a reservation block as a team template (tags + description).
- Audit trail: every drag/resize should append a human-readable entry ("Priya adjusted GPU count from 6 -> 4") to reservation history.

Anything missing? Ping in #console-ux.
